title: OFAC Designates Exchange Houses and Companies in Iran-Linked Rahbar Network
summary: On November 23, 2026, OFAC designated Iranian exchange houses in the rahbar network. Nine appear in leaked records; seven placed over 5,300 payment orders.
body_markdown:
## The nine entities at a glance


TRM analysis of entities sanctioned by OFAC that also appear in a leaked rahbar payment ledger.


The license dates in the summary table come from the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism license search, checked in November 2026. The search lists license dates only, not owners.


## What a rahbar company does


Rahbar companies are affiliates of Iranian banks that manage networks of exchange houses and front companies to move foreign currency for the bank’s clients. The November 23, 2026 Treasury release describes rahbar companies as bank affiliates that manage sanctions-evasion networks for their Iran-based clients, and says the Central Bank of Iran oversees the wider shadow banking system.


The targets of OFAC’s latest action parallel entities contained in a recent report by WikiIran, which describes itself as a project run by anti-regime professionals in exile. Earlier this month, the site leaked multiple files under the title “The Rahbar Records.” TRM analyzed the files in November 2026. They include a payment ledger of 12,092 orders registered between March 25, 2025 and July 16, 2026. Each order names a payer, a beneficiary, a currency, and an amount. The ledger captures payment instructions, not settlements.


TRM cannot independently verify every document in the leak. However, OFAC’s earlier actions against the same network match the files in at least four places. A staff list in the files names all seven employees of Farab Soroush Afagh Qeshm Company (FSAQ), the Shahr Bank rahbar company, whom OFAC designated on October 15, 2026, and national identification numbers in the list match OFAC’s for six of the seven.[OFAC designated Oviedo Overseas Company Limited and Cailafang Pte. Ltd. (opens in a new tab)](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0596) on August 7, 2026. The ledger records five payment orders to Oviedo between June 3 and July 6, 2026, and six to Cailafang from November 1, 2025.[OFAC designated Elitesphere Trading Co., Limited (opens in a new tab)](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261015) on October 15, 2026 as a Hong Kong company used by FSAQ to move funds, and the ledger records eight orders to it from six payers between May 9 and December 27, 2025.


## The designated payers


Seven designated entities appear as payers in the ledger. Treasury describes all of them as Dubai front companies in the rahbar network, except Bogazici, which is based in Turkey.


Payment orders placed by each designated payer, March 25, 2025 to July 16, 2026. Order counts exclude two orders with outlier amounts. Source: TRM analysis of a leaked Rahbar payment ledger.


Monthly payment orders from the seven designated payers combined. Orders without a payment date are excluded. Order counts exclude two orders with outlier amounts. Source: TRM analysis of a leaked Rahbar payment ledger .


##
Payments after designation


The ledger records two cases in which designated payers placed orders for companies OFAC had already designated.


Hemraj placed one order for USD 1,507,723.79 on June 12, 2025, to Hero Companion Limited. OFAC designated Hero Companion on June 6, 2025, six days earlier.


Dexterous placed five orders on October 29, 2025, totaling 1,179,283.00 United Arab Emirates dirhams (AED), to Crimson Blue Trading Co., Limited. Another payer placed a sixth on November 1, 2025, and the six together total AED 1,752,860.24. OFAC designated Crimson Blue on October 9, 2025, 20 days before the first order and 23 days before the last.


Payment orders to Hero Companion Limited and Crimson Blue Trading Co., Limited relative to OFAC’s designation of each. Orders on the same day are stacked. Source: TRM analysis of a leaked Rahbar payment ledger.


**


## Two large cash payout records


OGA Global registered a cash payout of USD 10 million on June 20, 2026. Grand Target registered a cash payout of USD 3 million on July 16, 2026, the last day listed in the ledger. The November 23 release says OGA Global General Trading LLC has overseen millions of dollars’ worth of payments for the National Iranian Tanker Company, which operates Iran’s fleet of state-owned oil tankers.


## Mellat Exchange Company


A broker register dated July 22, 2026 in the same leak lists 42 brokers with cumulative turnover in euro equivalent. It records about EUR 6.4 billion in cumulative turnover for Mellat Exchange. When TRM analyzed the register in November 2026, Mellat Exchange was not on the OFAC, UK, or EU sanctions lists. OFAC designated Mellat Exchange Company, together with three officials, in the action announced November 23, 2026. The release names Mahmoud Akhlaghi, Parviz Fazlju, and Mohammad Hossein Abbasi as officials of Mellat Exchange Company.


## Khore Al Hilal Goods Wholesalers Trading LLC


TRM analysis of leaked mail from Opal Exchange, which OFAC designated on May 1, 2026, identified one letter, dated March 10, 2024, that carries a Khore Al Hilal letterhead and announces a deposit of AED 15 million to an account at Bank Melli Iran’s Dubai branch. Internal TRM analysis has previously documented the same activity involving settlement documents naming Iranian banks. OFAC designated Khore Al Hilal in the action announced November 23, 2026. The release says Khore Al Hilal Goods Wholesalers Trading LLC has been used extensively by Opal Exchange, also known as Pedram Pirouzan Exchange, and Omid Sepah Exchange to move millions of dollars for Bank Sepah.


## What this means for compliance teams


The designated companies share a profile that the Treasury release and the ledger both describe. They are trading companies in Dubai, Hong Kong, and Turkey that appear as payers or counterparties for Iranian exchange houses and banks. Several received a license shortly before their first order, or after an earlier license had lapsed.


Teams screening counterparties can act on three points:


- Screen the entities and their aliases against the updated SDN list, and review prior payments from or to them
- Review trade and exchange-house counterparties in the UAE, Hong Kong, and Turkey for sudden volume, recent licenses, and general-trading descriptions that do not match the payment flows
- Look for payments dated after a beneficiary’s designation date, because the ledger shows they can appear in payment records


TRM’s analysis of the broader network is ongoing.
